passages.sermon:
This is a song.
People sing this song while going up to Jerusalem.
The song is called a song of ascents.

passages.text: Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth— let Israel now declare— many a time they have persecuted me from my youth, but they have not prevailed against me.
passages.sermon:
This is a song of ascents.
Israel speaks in this song.
Israel says, “Many times people have persecuted me since I was young.”
Israel repeats, “Many times people have persecuted me since I was young.”
But my enemies have not defeated me.
They have not overcome me.
passages.original: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרַ֑י יֹֽאמַר־ נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרָ֑י גַּ֝ם לֹא־ יָ֥כְלוּ לִֽי׃

passages.text: The plowmen plowed over my back; they made their furrows long.
passages.sermon:
Israel speaks in this song of ascents.
Enemies attacked Israel many times since youth.
They caused deep suffering.
They acted like plowmen.
They plowed over Israel’s back.
They made their furrows long.
Their oppression was harsh and lasting.
passages.original: עַל־ גַּ֭בִּי חָרְשׁ֣וּ חֹרְשִׁ֑ים הֶ֝אֱרִ֗יכוּ לְמַעֲנוֹתָם׃

passages.text: The LORD is righteous; He has cut me from the cords of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is righteous.
The LORD acts justly.
The LORD has cut me free from the cords of the wicked.
The LORD has broken the bonds that evil people put on me.
The LORD rescues me from those who do wrong.

passages.text: May all who hate Zion be turned back in shame.
passages.sermon:
This is a prayer about Zion.
Zion is the city of God.
Some people hate Zion.
May all who hate Zion feel shame.
May all who hate Zion turn back.
May God cause their plans to fail.
passages.original: יֵ֭בֹשׁוּ וְיִסֹּ֣גוּ אָח֑וֹר כֹּ֝֗ל שֹׂנְאֵ֥י צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can grow, unable to fill the hands of the reaper, or the arms of the binder of sheaves.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about those who hate Zion.
He asks that they become like grass on rooftops.
Grass on rooftops grows quickly but dries up before it matures.
This grass withers before it can be harvested.
It does not fill the hands of the reaper.
It does not fill the arms of the one who gathers sheaves.
passages.original: יִ֭הְיוּ כַּחֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֑וֹת שֶׁקַּדְמַ֖ת שָׁלַ֣ף יָבֵֽשׁ׃ שֶׁלֹּ֤א מִלֵּ֖א כַפּ֥וֹ קוֹצֵ֗ר וְחִצְנ֥וֹ מְעַמֵּֽר׃

passages.text: May none who pass by say to them, “The blessing of the LORD be on you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about people who hate Zion.
It describes a curse for these people.
No one who passes by them will speak a blessing.
No one will say, “The blessing of the LORD be on you.”
No one will say, “We bless you in the name of the LORD.”
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א אָֽמְר֨וּ׀ הָעֹבְרִ֗ים בִּרְכַּֽת־ יְהוָ֥ה אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם בֵּרַ֥כְנוּ אֶ֝תְכֶ֗ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃
